findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Once the manager signs the stipend request and finance confirms the budget line, the request moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The sentence has confusing word order that obscures the sequence of actions. "once the manager signs it, after finance confirms" creates ambiguity about what happens first.

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes."
findings.fix: Move the confirmation email sentence to follow "final processing" and clarify the actual sequence: confirmation email is sent, employee reviews it, then submits the final request.
findings.violation: The narrative sequence is backwards. The text says processing finishes before the employee submits, but then describes reviewing and submitting after that.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify the trigger: "The requester gets an automatic reminder three days after the request is marked incomplete."
findings.violation: The trigger for the three-day reminder is unclear. It is not stated whether it counts from when the request was submitted or from when it was marked incomplete.

findings.evidence: "Employees keep proof of purchase for every stipend item. A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests. Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Clarify what counts as proof: "Employees may submit a photo of the receipt for approval. The original receipt must be retained for one year after the purchase date."
findings.violation: There is a contradiction between "a photo of the receipt is enough" and "must retain receipts." It is unclear whether employees must keep the physical receipt or only the photo.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite to match the document voice: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a photo check of the equipment once per year."
findings.location: Line 45, shift in voice and audience
findings.violation: The shift from third person to second person ("You") and first person plural ("we") is inconsistent with the rest of the policy and leaves unclear who is being addressed.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Additionally" or remove it entirely. The sentence can stand on its own.
findings.violation: "Similarly" does not logically connect this statement to the previous sentence about photo checks.

findings.evidence: In "Terminology Notes" section: "Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Delete these sentences from "Terminology Notes" and ensure they appear only in "Approval Timeline."
findings.location: Lines 52-53, duplicate content in wrong section
findings.violation: This duplicates information from the "Approval Timeline" section and appears in a section meant for defining terminology, not process steps.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence is a fragment. "confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt" is not a complete construction.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.violation: These three sentences are unrelated to the home-office equipment stipend policy and appear to be copy-pasted from another document.

findings.evidence: Line 6: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit." Line 73: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit." (repeated verbatim)
findings.fix: Remove one instance of the duplicated sentence.
findings.violation: The sentence appears twice in the same document in different sections, creating redundancy.
